name: shell

build.// cache: Cacheable here rather than via a targetDefault: `serve` uses the SAME executor and is continuous, so an executor-keyed default sets cache on it too and Nx rejects that. Outputs name the whole dist/apps/<app> directory, not just browser/ — a restore that recreates part of it is worse than no cache, because the deploy would upload it.
build.// inputs: federatedTemplates: Tailwind scans the whole workspace, but ONLY the shell's stylesheet is ever loaded into the page — Native Federation ships a remote's chunks, never its CSS. So a utility class first used in a remote template exists at runtime only if the SHELL was rebuilt. Without this input the shell stays cached across remote edits and the class silently does not exist in production. Found when overflow-x-auto, added to audit-logs, computed as visible.

esbuild.// inputs: Mirrors build: this is the target that actually compiles the stylesheet, and the @angular/build:application targetDefault would otherwise cache it on production inputs alone.

options.command: pnpm exec concurrently -k -s first -n SERVE,LH -c magenta,blue "pnpm exec nx run-many -t serve-static -p shell,iam,feature-flags,audit-logs" "pnpm exec wait-on --timeout 120000 http://localhost:4200 http://localhost:4201/remoteEntry.json http://localhost:4202/remoteEntry.json http://localhost:4203/remoteEntry.json && node tools/lighthouse/run.mjs --runs 3"

lighthouse.// command: wait-on carries an explicit --timeout because its default is infinite. When shell:build fails, serve-static has nothing to serve, 4200 never binds, and run-many keeps the other three continuous servers alive — so concurrently never sees anything exit either. The gate could not fail, only hang, and it hid a real build failure for nine minutes twice.

// implicitDependencies: Nx cannot see a CSS @import, so the dependency on the design tokens is invisible to the project graph. Without this edge a colour change is 'affected: nothing' and skips every axe, contrast and build gate that exists to judge it.
